subject: Contract uplift playbook + QBR slot request
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara@heliohealth.com>, Jacob Li <jli@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Contract uplift playbook + QBR slot request

Hi Sara / Jacob —

Following our renewal signal last week, I wanted to kick off a short playbook to align on the contract uplift, expected capacity increases, and a QBR scheduling window so our teams can scope the Dedicated capacity uplift and run the onboarding plan. High-level asks from our side:  

- Confirm target start date for increased throughput (we typically see customers pick the start of the next quarter).
- Share an estimated 3-month token/day profile (attachments can be fine) so we can recommend quantization and batching knobs.
- Pick two 60-minute QBR slots in the next 10 business days for exec + technical alignment.

Proposed timeline (working draft):
1) This week — intake call and data point collection
2) Next week — Redwood provides draft Mutual Action Plan with capacity & pricing options
3) Two weeks — procurement review and DocuSign routing
4) Goal: capacity live within 4–6 weeks after sign-off (dedicated nodes or hybrid burst)

For QBR slots, could you do either:
- Tue 2027-05-04, 11:00–12:00 PT
- Thu 2027-05-06, 09:00–10:00 PT

I attached a short deal summary and a template for capacity estimates to speed things up. Ben will lead the technical plan; Monica will help with contract ops. Vivek will be on point for any regional SLA clarifications.

Thanks — looking forward to your availability.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin | Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Jensen <sara@heliohealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Li <jli@heliohealth.com>, procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract uplift playbook + QBR slot request

Chloe —

Thanks for the clear plan. We want to move deliberately but quickly here. A couple of notes from my side:

- We are targeting an internal go-live for the expanded features around 2027-06-15, so the capacity start ideally would be week of 2027-06-14.
- I attached a quick-ballpark capacity estimate (token/day by environment): you'll see our spike pattern during end-of-month processing.
- For the QBR, Tue 2027-05-04 11:00 PT works for our execs. Prefer that slot.

Two asks for Redwood: 1) can you confirm how the dedicated nodes handle weekend batch spikes (KV-cache persistency / prefix caching behavior)? 2) we need a preliminary TCO for the three options (hosted burst, dedicated baseline, dedicated + burst).

I'll loop procurement on the DocuSign routing once we have the Mutual Action Plan.

— Sara
Sara Jensen | Head of Platform Integrations
HelioHealth
Attachments: Helio_capacity_estimate.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara@heliohealth.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract uplift playbook + QBR slot request

Sara — thanks for the quick reply and the capacity snapshot. I pulled the attachment into a short MOP (runbook) and sketched three recommended paths: hosted-burst, reserved-dedicated, and hybrid (reserved baseline + burst capacity). Key callouts:  

- Weekend spikes: With Dedicated we persist KV cache across warm nodes for the same model family; that reduces cold-start token cost by ~40–60% on typical Helio patterns. We'll include cache warmup steps in the onboarding runbook.
- TCO: attached a one-page Redwood_deal_summary.pdf showing per-token and per-hour math for each path and an initial uplift estimate at 10%/30%/50% uplift bands.
- Risk: If you plan sustained 30% uplift, reserved capacity is materially cheaper after 6 weeks; short bursts favor hosted-burst.

Next steps for the QBR on Tue 2027-05-04 11:00 PT: Chloe will send a calendar invite with agenda; please add any internal stakeholders (ops, security). We'll use that call to lock the Mutual Action Plan and target sign-off date.

Attachments: Redwood_deal_summary.pdf, Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

Chloe / Ben —

Confirmed: Tue 2027-05-04 11:00 PT on our calendars. I've added Jacob (platform ops) and procurement in cc. Procurement flagged two items they want on the Mutual Action Plan: data retention options and a clear SLA fallback during the migration window. Can you include a short section on those in the MAP?
